# The release path's orphan and broad-stage guards have no spec

Sub of #17922 · sibling of #17924, #17964, #18052 · the third of #17922's owed residual rows

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-09-03T13:59:34Z; no equivalent found. A2A claim sweep over the last 30 messages (all read-states) at 13:45Z, plus my own `[lane-claim]` on this exact row at 13:48Z: no competing claim. Memory Core rationale sweep on the problem's nouns (deleted release-note orphan guard, broad-staging witness) returned no prior decision on this row beyond #17922's own ruling. Own-assignment sweep: 13 open tickets assigned to me, none covering the release path's coverage.

## Context

`c623b2f63c` (#17791 via #17806) deleted 804 unit spec files on the `test/playwright/unit/ai/**` path prefix. #17922 censused the 30 under `ai/buildScripts/` and found **27 whose subject never left this repository**. 21 recovered verbatim in #17924 / PR #17925; `DataSyncPipeline` came back via #17920 / #17927; `WorkflowScopeClassifier` via #18052 / #18053; `check-theme-surfaces` via #18162 / #18163.

Re-measured at `dev@f6c7a0c360`, #17922's owed set is **3**, not the 4 its body still states — the `check-theme-surfaces` row reads as *"in flight — PR #18163, awaiting review"* and that PR merged at 09:29Z today. This ticket takes one of the three: `release/PublishReleaseNoteOrphan.spec.mjs`, 171 lines, 6 arms.

## The Problem

The subject is `buildScripts/release/publish.mjs` — 281 lines at HEAD, the operator-invoked release entrypoint, protected by §critical_gates 8. It never left. Four of its six deleted arms guard properties that are live today with no witness at all:

| unguarded property | consequence if it silently breaks |
|---|---|
| the staging note is removed only AFTER `gh release create` reads it | the release is cut from a file the script already deleted, or the staging copy lingers |
| no top-level `release-notes/v*.md` survives beside its `chunk-N` mirror | the version double-lists in the release index and the sitemap |
| the orphan predicate distinguishes a pre-publish staging note from a post-publish duplicate | either the designed staging state reads as a defect, or the defect reads as staging |
| each release leaf appears once in `apps/portal/resources/data/releases.json` | the reader sees the duplicate the orphan class produces |

Two more arms asserted through `ai/scripts/lifecycle/postReleaseSync.mjs`, which correctly departed. #17922's disposition ruling (2026-09-02) decided both per arm rather than per file: the handoff arm **re-aims** onto the ordering invariant that survives, and the broad-stage arm keeps its **Engine half**, with its Brain half named as a custody transfer owed to `neomjs/neo-agent-brain` rather than dropped.

The broad-stage half is the sharpest of the four live properties. `publish.mjs:155` stages with `git add .` and `:154` is `assertNoArchiveLogicalIdentityCollisions(...)`. Every commit on the release path runs `--no-verify` by design, so husky and the `lint-staged` copy of that guard are structurally blind to it, and proving the ordering behaviourally would require cutting a release. A source-ordering assertion is the only available instrument, and there is none.

## The Architectural Reality

- Placement is the surviving sibling tree `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/**` (17 specs at HEAD), **not** the deleted `unit/ai/buildScripts/**` path. The `ai/` prefix is what classified the file as extracted substrate and would re-arm the same deletion at the next boundary change. This contradicts `.agents/skills/unit-test/references/unit-test.md` §7, which still routes `buildScripts` specs to `unit/ai/buildScripts/`; that is stale substrate and is out of scope here.
- The arms read sources rather than importing them: `publish.mjs` is a top-level release script whose module scope runs `main()`, so a source-text assertion is the honest instrument, matching the restored `WorkflowScopeClassifier.spec.mjs` precedent.
- The release-index arm's subject is generated: `buildScripts/docs/index/release.mjs` writes `releases.json`, and its line 138 deliberately omits `isLeaf` on release nodes.

## The Fix

1. Restore the spec to `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/release/`.
2. Re-aim the handoff arm: drop the `ai:post-release-sync` script resolution (that script is absent from `package.json`), keep the ordering half, and assert the print names the Brain-side checkout — a beat that does not say where the next step runs is not a handoff.
3. Reduce the broad-stage arm to its Engine half, keeping the per-file pinning (never a total) so a second unguarded broad stage cannot arrive and still pass, and name the Brain-side custody transfer in the file.
4. **Repair the release-index arm, which cannot fail as written.** It filters `node.isLeaf`; the generator omits that field on release leaves, so the filter matches **0 of 174** nodes — and 0 at `c623b2f63c~1` as well, so this is not split drift: the arm was already vacuous when it was deleted. Select a leaf by the property that distinguishes one, assert the population is non-empty so it cannot silently re-vacuate, and check `path` alongside `id`.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/release/PublishReleaseNoteOrphan.spec.mjs` | #17922 AC-1; sibling precedent `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/WorkflowScopeClassifier.spec.mjs` | 6 arms over `publish.mjs`, the release-notes corpus and `releases.json` | none — a release path with no witness is the defect | spec header | each arm red against a seeded mutation of its own subject |
| the release-index leaf predicate | `buildScripts/docs/index/release.mjs:131,138` | a leaf is a node pointing at a release-note file; the population is asserted non-empty | n/a | spec JSDoc | red when the index is stripped of leaves, which the pre-repair arm could not see |

## Decision Record impact

`none` — restoring Engine-owned coverage to the Engine is what ADR 0040 §2.3 already prescribes (the ADR lives in `neo-agent-brain`, not here; its absence from `learn/agentos/decisions/` is not evidence).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `PublishReleaseNoteOrphan.spec.mjs` exists under `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/release/` and passes against its HEAD subjects.
- [ ] Every arm is shown **red** against a seeded mutation of its own subject, and each mutation reddens only its own arm — a restored spec that cannot fail is not restored coverage. Mutations must cover, at minimum: the staging-note removal moved before the release, a lingering post-publish duplicate, a neutered orphan predicate, a twice-listed release leaf, an index with no leaves at all, a deleted handoff print, a handoff that names no destination, and a broad stage moved before its guard.
- [ ] The file names both re-aimed arms and the reason, so the difference from the deleted original is auditable rather than invisible.
- [ ] The release-index arm's vacuity is stated with the measurement from **both** trees, so it cannot read as split drift.
- [ ] The Brain-side broad-stage half is named in the spec as a custody transfer, not silently absent.
- [ ] The `unit` project's collected spec-file count rises by exactly 1, measured by count and not by a green run.
- [ ] #17922's body is corrected so its `check-theme-surfaces` row no longer reads as in flight.

## Out of Scope

- **The other two owed rows** — `RebuildContentIndexesAndSeo` and `WorkflowConcurrency` stay with #17922, unclaimed. `WorkflowConcurrency` is the sharpest of them: its subject runs on every PR.
- **Filing the Brain-side witness.** The ordering invariant in `ai/scripts/lifecycle/postReleaseSync.mjs` has no spec in the repository that owns it. That is a `neomjs/neo-agent-brain` filing with its own sweep, and #17922's ruling deliberately declined to file it from inside this arc.
- **Changing what `publish.mjs` does.** Restoration is not the moment to fix the subject; both call sites are correctly ordered at HEAD and this ticket reports no live defect in them.
- **`unit-test.md` §7's stale placement rule.** Real friction, wrong repository — the skill corpus is `neomjs/neo-agent-skills` substrate.
